_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Equatorial Guinea covering Bubi and Fang peoples, Portuguese discovery, Spanish colonial period (Fernando Pó and Río Muni), independence 1968, Macías Nguema's reign of terror, Obiang Nguema (world's longest-ruling non-royal head of state), and oil wealth/corruption.

country_profile.capital: Malabo (current), Ciudad de la Paz (planned new capital on mainland)

ethnic_groups.name: Fang
ethnic_groups.notes: Dominant on mainland (Río Muni); Bantu people; Nguema family's ethnic group; sub-groups include Ntumu and Okak

ethnic_groups.name: Bubi
ethnic_groups.notes: Indigenous people of Bioko Island; pre-Fang inhabitants; distinct Bantu language and culture

ethnic_groups.name: Ndowe/Playeros
ethnic_groups.notes: Coastal mainland peoples; include Combe, Benga, Bapuku, and Balengue

ethnic_groups.name: Annobonés
ethnic_groups.notes: Inhabitants of Annobón Island; Creole Portuguese speakers; mixed African-Portuguese heritage

ethnic_groups.name: Bisio/Bujeba
ethnic_groups.notes: Small mainland group near Gabonese border

ethnic_groups.name: Fernandino
ethnic_groups.notes: Creole community of Bioko; descended from freed slaves and Sierra Leonean Krio settlers; English-speaking heritage

natural_resources.notes: Oil boom since 1990s transformed economy; highest GDP per capita in Africa ($20k+) but 70% live in poverty (inequality extreme); Marathog/Zafiro/Ceiba oil fields; gas (LNG plant at Punta Europa); timber exports declining; oil production past peak and declining rapidly

military.notes: Presidential Guard (Moroccan-trained) most capable; 2004 Wonga coup attempt (Mark Thatcher/Simon Mann plot); security handled by Moroccan/Israeli advisors; militia loyal to Obiang family

debt_aid.notes: Oil wealth means minimal foreign aid; Teodorin Obiang (VP/son) luxury spending scandals ($100M Malibu mansion, $30M Bugatti collection, seized by France/Swiss); money laundering investigations globally; economy contracting as oil declines

education.notes: High nominal literacy (95%) but education quality poor; Spanish-language instruction (only Spanish-speaking African nation); French also official; scholarships to Spain/Cuba; limited domestic higher education; oil wealth not translated to education quality

diaspora_migration.notes: Spanish exile community (fled Macías regime 1970s); net emigration despite oil wealth (inequality drives departure); Cameroonians/Nigerians work in oil sector; Fang ethnic ties cross borders with Cameroon/Gabon

digital_economy.notes: Very limited digital economy; GETESA monopoly telecom; expensive/slow internet; no meaningful tech scene; oil wealth not diversified into tech; Sipopo (new capital area) has modern infrastructure but limited digital economy

country_profile.notes_unique: The only African country with Spanish as an official language; oil wealth gives it Africa's highest GDP per capita, though wealth distribution is extremely unequal.

current_leader.name: Teodoro Obiang Nguema Mbasogo
current_leader.title: President
current_leader.notes: World's longest-serving current head of state; overthrew uncle Macías Nguema; son Teodorín groomed as successor

prime_minister.name: Manuela Roka Botey
prime_minister.notes: First female PM of Equatorial Guinea

former_leaders.name: Francisco Macías Nguema
former_leaders.notes: First president; reign of terror killed ~50,000 (a third of the population); executed after Obiang's coup

910.name: Early Peoples: Bubi and Pygmy Inhabitants
910.description: Bubi people settle the island of Bioko (Fernando Pó) from the mainland; Pygmy communities inhabit the continental rainforest (Río Muni).

sub_clusters.name: Bubi Settlement of Bioko
sub_clusters.description: Bantu-speaking Bubi people migrate to Bioko island from the Cameroon coast; develop distinct culture, yam agriculture, and chieftaincy system isolated from the mainland.

sub_clusters.name: Pygmy Forest Peoples of Río Muni
sub_clusters.description: BaKa and other Pygmy groups inhabit the equatorial rainforest of the continental region; hunter-gatherer economy; later displaced by Fang migration.

920.name: Fang Migration into Río Muni
920.description: The Fang people migrate southward into the continental territory (Río Muni); warrior culture and decentralised clan-based society.

sub_clusters.name: Fang Expansion and Settlement
sub_clusters.description: Fang clans migrate from the Sanaga River region (Cameroon) southward through the equatorial forest; displace or absorb earlier inhabitants; establish village-based chiefdoms.

sub_clusters.name: Fang Social Organisation and Bieri
sub_clusters.description: Fang develop elaborate ancestor worship (Bieri reliquary figures); segmentary lineage system; long-distance trade in ivory and forest products.

930.name: Portuguese Discovery and Early European Contact
930.description: Portuguese navigator Fernão do Pó discovers Bioko 1471; island used for slave trade; Treaty of El Pardo transfers territories to Spain.

sub_clusters.name: Discovery of Fernando Pó
sub_clusters.description: Fernão do Pó reaches the island 1471; Portuguese establish limited presence; sugar plantations attempted; Bubi resist colonisation.

sub_clusters.name: Treaty of El Pardo (1778)
sub_clusters.description: Portugal cedes Fernando Pó and Annobón to Spain in exchange for South American territories; Spain largely neglects the islands initially.

940.name: Spanish Guinea (1843–1968)
940.description: Spain establishes effective control; British anti-slavery base at Clarence (Malabo); cocoa plantations with contract labour; Río Muni acquired; decolonisation.

sub_clusters.name: British Anti-Slavery Base and Clarence
sub_clusters.description: Britain leases Fernando Pó as anti-slave-trade naval base; founds Clarence (now Malabo); freed slaves (Fernandinos/Krio) settle; Spain reasserts control 1855.

sub_clusters.name: Spanish Cocoa Plantation Economy
sub_clusters.description: Cocoa plantations dominate Fernando Pó; Bubi dispossessed; contract labourers imported from Nigeria, Liberia, and Río Muni; Fernandino Creole elite.

sub_clusters.name: Río Muni Colonisation
sub_clusters.description: Spain pacifies the Fang interior of Río Muni; coffee and timber extraction; far less developed than Fernando Pó; colonial neglect.

sub_clusters.name: Decolonisation and Self-Government
sub_clusters.description: UN pressure forces Spain to grant autonomy 1963; pre-independence elections; Macías Nguema wins presidential election October 1968.

950.name: Macías Nguema: Reign of Terror (1968–1979)
950.description: Francisco Macías Nguema establishes one of Africa's most brutal dictatorships; mass executions, forced labour, and international isolation; one-third of population flees or is killed.

sub_clusters.name: Macías Nguema's Consolidation
sub_clusters.description: Macías abolishes constitution; declares himself president for life; anti-Spanish and anti-intellectual purges; Nigerian labourers expelled from cocoa plantations.

sub_clusters.name: The Terror: Mass Killings and Economic Collapse
sub_clusters.description: Estimated 50,000–80,000 killed; education banned; churches closed; country described as 'Africa's Dachau'; economy collapses; electricity and infrastructure disintegrate.

sub_clusters.name: Overthrow and Execution of Macías
sub_clusters.description: Nephew Teodoro Obiang Nguema Mbasogo leads military coup August 1979; Macías tried and executed; Obiang takes power.

960.name: Obiang Nguema Era (1979–Present)
960.description: Teodoro Obiang Nguema Mbasogo becomes the world's longest-serving non-royal head of state; oil discovery transforms economy; massive corruption and human rights abuses persist.

sub_clusters.name: Obiang Pre-Oil Period
sub_clusters.description: Obiang maintains authoritarian control; cosmetic reforms; Spanish and French aid; cocoa economy stagnates; discovery of oil at Zafiro field 1995 transforms prospects.

sub_clusters.name: Oil Boom and Kleptocracy
sub_clusters.description: Equatorial Guinea becomes Africa's third-richest country per capita; oil revenues captured by Obiang family; son 'Teodorín' convicted of corruption in France; vast inequality.

sub_clusters.name: Wonga Coup Attempt (2004)
sub_clusters.description: Mark Thatcher-linked mercenary plot to overthrow Obiang foiled; Simon Mann and others arrested in Zimbabwe and Equatorial Guinea; international scandal.

sub_clusters.name: Obiang Dynasty and Succession
sub_clusters.description: Obiang grooms son Teodoro Nguema Obiang Mangue ('Teodorín') as vice-president; longest-ruling non-royal leader globally; suppression of all opposition.
